title: A 3.47 NEF 175.2dB FOMs Direct Digitization Front-End Featuring Delta Amplification for Enhanced Dynamic Range and Energy Efficiency in Bio-Signal Acquisition
problem: Bio-signal acquisition (EEG, ExG) requires low input-referred noise (~50–60 nV/√Hz) but must reject large artifacts (100+ mV stimulation artifacts). Conventional LNA-based front-ends saturate under artifacts and require seconds to recover; ADC-first VCO-based DSM approaches achieve wide dynamic range but suffer 80–120 nV/√Hz noise (vs. 50–60 nV/√Hz requirement), due to noise-linearity tradeoff in first integrator.
motivation: Implantable/wearable bio-monitoring needs simultaneous low noise and high artifact immunity; existing front-ends sacrifice one for the other, limiting clinical viability.
method: The circuit uses a direct-to-digital approach with delta amplification—a circuit design that extends the input range—in the first stage, breaking the traditional tradeoff between low noise and artifact rejection. Instead of amplifying first and saturating under large artifacts, this keeps the signal linear across a wide range while a VCO-based delta-sigma modulator (an analog-to-digital converter) digitizes it. This enables the front-end to reject 100+ millivolt artifact spikes while maintaining 50-60 nanovolts per square root Hertz noise, and achieves a 3.47 NEF (noise efficiency factor).
key_novelty: Delta amplification in an ADC-first VCO-based converter simultaneously achieves low noise (3.47 NEF) and high dynamic range (handling 100+ millivolt artifacts) for bio-signal recording.
contributions: Direct digitization front-end with 50–60 nV/√Hz input-referred noise (ExG spec compliant)
3.47 NEF and 175.2 dB FoMs demonstrate energy efficiency
Enhanced dynamic range rejects 100+ mV stimulation artifacts without saturation
Delta amplification reduces noise-linearity tradeoff in first integrator

metrics.other: NEF 3.47, FoMs 175.2 dB, IRN 50–60 nV/√Hz, dynamic range >100 mV

baselines: VCO-based DSM ADC-first designs (higher noise ~80–120 nV/√Hz)
limitations: Sampling rate, bandwidth, and common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) not specified.
